newsitem.title: USA: Triteal cites shortfall on inability to close sale.
newsitem.headline: Triteal cites shortfall on inability to close sale.

text.p: TriTeal Corp said Wednesday it expects its earnings to fall below analysts' expectations because the company did not close a $2 million sale with a government reseller.

TriTeal said it expects to report a net loss for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997 ranging from approximately $900,000 to $1.2 million, or $0.09 to $0.12 per share vs a net loss of $644,000, or $0.10 per share, for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.

TriTeal expects revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997 to be in the range of about $4.6 million to $4.9 million, compared to $3.8 million in revenue reported for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.

Revenue for the year ended March 31, 1997, is estimated to be from $15.7 million to $16 million, compared with revenue of $8.2 million reported for fiscal 1996. For fiscal 1997, the company expects to report a net loss ranging from about $1.9 million to $2.2 million, or between $.23 and $.26 per share, compared with a net loss of $4.8 million, or $.72 per share, for fiscal 1996.

"As we have stated in the past, because our revenue typically consists of large orders, the loss of any individual order could have significant impact on quarterly results." said TriTeal Chairman and Chief Executive Jeff Witous. "However, we are committed to making adjustments designed to mitigate future risk associated with large orders."
